task.description: WF-02 Step 1b RE-GATE (rework attempt 2 of 3, last allowed under the ceiling) for REQ-376. Narrow scope: verify this rework's claimed fix to SS4.4b's previously-cited unbounded-reconciliation defect (v2 FAIL) -- real structural smallness argument, concrete bounded batching mechanism, explicit lock-footprint tie to EO-001, a new open question (OQ7) -- and spot-check SS4.3/4.3.1 (crash recovery), FINALIZE handling, and AC2's framing were not altered by this narrow rework. Also verify the batch loop's interaction with SS4.3.1's crash-recovery state machine (mid-loop crash re-entry: no double-processing, no orphaned state).
acceptance_criteria: a decision record resolving Postgres-native monthly PARTITION BY RANGE (created_at) for events/events_archive exists under docs/migration/decisions/, cross-references 0003 Decision C and ISS-0014, and carries REVIEWER sign-off (pending -- see decision record's own Sign-off section)

retiring one month of expired history is designed as a short whole-partition DDL sequence (DETACH/ATTACH, not row-by-row DELETE), honestly stated as a sequence rather than mislabeled as one statement, with idempotent crash-recovery/resume via catalog state, an explicit stuck-pending-detach error case, and a stated test shape proving no per-row DELETE runs in the retirement steps, the platform accepts a concurrent write throughout (EO-001), and a crash mid-sequence can be resumed correctly

the protected-record (keep_forever-policy) exemption mechanism is specified, with a stated test shape proving the count is identical before/after retiring a month containing at least one protected record (EO-002)
the architectural mechanism making an already-retired month's process-instance history still replay with no gap is specified (EO-003)
the pre-creation mechanism is specified such that no test or code path ever waits on partition creation while a write is in flight

the relationship between the new mechanism and Letflow.EventStore.archive/1's existing row-level move is stated explicitly (coexist, with archive/1 unchanged) in both the decision record and the design doc
every acceptance criterion maps to a concrete design element -- no TBD; open questions listed explicitly instead

result.summary:
Read SS4.4b, SS5, and SS7's new OQ7 directly in the current file (not the rework's self-report), plus SS4.3/SS4.3.1/SS4.3.2/SS4.3.3 and the AC2 framing paragraph for regression, plus decision record 0037 for consistency. All five specifically-requested checks hold:

(1) Real structural argument for non-smallness, honestly contrasted against 4.4a: the 'Why this population is not assumed small (unlike 4.4a's keep_forever rows)' paragraph (line ~442) explicitly states keep_forever's smallness is 'justified by design' (the deliberate exception case) while 4.4b's population 'receives *every* row archive/1 moves for this month' across the whole (deliberately long, per SS4.2) min_partition_age_days window, and 'scales with this tenant's actual archived-event volume' -- a structural argument, not a bare assertion, and it does not merely repeat 4.4a's rarity logic.

(2) Concrete, bounded, well-formed batching mechanism: new config knob reconciliation_batch_size (default 5000, same config location/pattern as min_partition_age_days), one Repo.transaction/1 per batch, loop body is SELECT ... ORDER BY created_at, event_id LIMIT <batch_size> (no OFFSET) then INSERT into the still-attached events_y<year>m<month> + DELETE from events_archive_default for the returned ids, terminating when a SELECT returns fewer than batch_size rows. Traced the logic: since each batch's DELETE physically removes exactly the rows just SELECTed before the next iteration's SELECT runs (synchronous, same process, no concurrency within the loop itself), the next SELECT naturally returns the next slice with no OFFSET needed -- this is correct and terminates for a static input set. The DELETE's 'event_id = ANY(...) AND created_at = ANY(...)' predicate (two independent ANY arrays rather than a composite/tuple match) is not a new bug: event_id is the table's globally-unique-per-row key component (confirmed against the codebase's existing archive_phase1_insert/archive_phase2_delete idiom in lib/letflow/event_store.ex, which filters by event_id alone), so the created_at clause is redundant-but-harmless, not incorrect.

(3) Lock footprint tied explicitly to EO-001: the 'Bound checked against SS5's EO-001 non-blocking claim' paragraph (line ~485) states each batch transaction takes only row-level locks on the batch_size rows being moved, never a lock on the events/events_archive parent relations or one conflicting with concurrent DML on any other partition/tenant, and states explicitly 'this per-batch lock footprint is constant, independent of the reconciled set's total size' -- naming the structural (per-transaction, not per-month) nature of the bound as the load-bearing difference from the prior failed revision.

(4) New OQ7 present (SS7, line ~673), explicitly analogous to OQ1: flags reconciliation_batch_size's default (5000) as picked with no production data, notes the reconciled population's size is itself unknown pending OQ4 (min_partition_age_days default), and scopes the open question to tuning/operational visibility, not correctness -- correctly distinguished from the per-batch bound, which SS4.4b states holds 'regardless of this number'.

(5) No regression: SS4.3 honest 'short SEQUENCE, not one statement' framing, SS4.3.1's four-state catalog-detected state machine (:not_started/:pending_detach/:detached_standalone/:already_retired), the FINALIZE recovery path and its own failure case ({:error, {:stuck_pending_detach, reason}}), and SS4.3.3's three crash-recovery test sub-cases all read identically in substance to the v2-passed revision -- SS4.3.3 step 1 now correctly references 'SS4.4, revised' and still states it 'runs only from :not_started', consistent with the new SS4.4 ordering note (4.4b before 4.4a). Decision record 0037 required no changes for this narrow fix and has none; still consistent with the design doc (relationship-to-archive/1 section unchanged, DETACH+ATTACH-never-DROP unchanged).

Crash-loop interaction (explicitly requested cross-check): traced the claim that 'a mid-loop crash just means already-relocated rows are absent from the next SELECT on retry, no new bookkeeping needed.' A crash during the SS4.4b loop occurs strictly before step 2's DETACH runs (the loop is part of step 1, which precedes DETACH), so catalog state after such a crash is still :not_started (still a child of events, inhdetachpending = false) -- confirmed against SS4.3.1's table and SS4.3.2's catalog-check definitions. A resumed retire_month/3 call therefore re-dispatches to :not_started and re-enters step 1 (SS4.4b then SS4.4a) from the top. Because each completed batch's DELETE already removed those rows from events_archive_default (moved, not copied) before the transaction committed, the resumed loop's first SELECT naturally returns only the not-yet-processed remainder -- no double-processing (already-moved rows can't be re-selected, since they're gone from the source table) and no orphaned state (no partial per-batch state survives outside the two tables' actual row membership, and SS4.3.1's 'catalog-detected, never self-persisted' design is not violated by the batch loop, which persists nothing of its own either). This claim is TRUE as stated and does not conflict with the ATTACH precondition, since ATTACH (step 4) only runs after DETACH (step 2), which only runs after step 1 (all of SS4.4b/4.4a) completes in full -- a mid-loop crash by definition never reaches step 2.

One architectural observation surfaced during this check but NOT used as FAIL grounds, since it is not new to this rework and was already implicitly present (and passed) in the v2-reviewed design: archive/1 continues running concurrently with retire_month/3 (per decision 0037's 'both mechanisms coexist' statement) and could in principle insert a fresh row into events_archive_default for the target month after SS4.4b's reconciliation loop completes but before step 4's ATTACH runs (steps 2-3 intervene) -- causing ATTACH's default-partition-emptiness precondition to fail; since SS4.3.1's :detached_standalone recovery path resumes at step 3, not step 1, a retry after such an ATTACH failure would not re-reconcile the new row and could fail identically on every retry. This is a pre-existing property of the whole DETACH/ATTACH-as-separate-non-transactional-steps architecture (unrelated to batching -- it existed identically when SS4.4b was a single unbounded transaction), not something this rework's batching fix introduced or was asked to address, and is outside this gate's narrow rework-2 scope. Flagging it here for ORCH/REVIEWER awareness, not as a gate defect.
result.advisory_note: Not a gate defect, no action required to pass this gate, but worth a REVIEWER or follow-up look at implementation time: a fresh archive/1 write landing in events_archive_default for the target month between SS4.4b's reconciliation completing and SS4.3 step 4's ATTACH (steps 2-3 intervene) can make ATTACH fail with no automatic recovery, since SS4.3.1's :detached_standalone resume path skips step 1 and goes straight to step 3. Pre-existing in the design since before this rework; not introduced by the SS4.4b batching fix.
